children.text: samprati madhuratiktakaṣāyāṇāṃ śītatvaṃ tathā kaṭvamlalavaṇānāṃ coṣṇatvaṃ tathā kaṭutiktakaṣāyāṇāṃ cāvṛṣyatvamityādayo rasadvāreṇa dravyāṇāṃ ye guṇā uktāstadapavādam āha teṣāmityādi ||
children.translated_text: Now, the coldness of sweet, bitter, and astringent tastes, the heat of pungent, sour, and salty tastes, and the non-aphrodisiac character of pungent, bitter, and astringent tastes, and so on: these properties of substances that have been stated through the medium of <s>rasa</s> (taste) are subject to exception. He states that exception with 'of these,' and so forth.

children.text: rasopadeśena rasaguṇakathanadvāreṇa dravyāṇāṃ yaḥ śītoṣṇādiguṇasaṃgrahaḥ kṛtaḥ sa vīryataḥ pākataścāviparītānāṃ teṣāṃ vakṣyamāṇakṣīrādidravyāṇāmeva nirdeṣṭuṃ śakyaḥ na tu rasaviparītavīryavipākānām ityarthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: The collection of qualities such as coldness and heat in substances, made by teaching <s>rasa</s> and by stating the qualities of tastes, can be specified only for those substances to be mentioned, such as milk, whose <s>vīrya</s> (potency) and <s>vipāka</s> (post-digestive effect) are not contrary. It is not meant for substances whose potency and post-digestive effect are contrary to their taste.
Among these, he teaches those whose potency and post-digestive effect are not contrary, with the words 'will be taught,' and so on.

children.text: upadekṣyata iti yathā paya ityādibhiḥ sambadhyate ||
children.translated_text: The phrase 'will be taught' is connected with expressions such as 'as, for example, milk.'

children.text: etāni hi dravyaguṇakathanaprasaṅge rasāviparītavīryavipākatayaivopadeṣṭavyānīti rasānurūpaguṇatvam eṣāṃ jñātavyam ityarthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: For, in the context of stating the qualities of substances, these substances are to be taught precisely as having potency and post-digestive effect not contrary to their tastes. Thus their taste-conformable qualities should be understood.

children.text: idaṃ tūdāharaṇaikadeśamātraṃ tenāparāṇy apyevaṃjātīyāny udāhartavyānītyāha evamādīnītyādi ||
children.translated_text: But this is only a single part of the examples. Therefore other things of the same kind too should be cited as examples. He states this with 'and so forth,' and so on.
'And so forth' means 'of this kind,' that is, wheat and the like.
